method: Actual PNGs opened with functions.view_image, including composed sheets of rendered files; implementation self-inspection, NOT formal review
source_camera_findings: Silo launch is deliberately tiny (Modern about7.75x15.96px at960x540), partly against the existing luminous well; exact world scale preserved.
Heavy incoming missile at .5s Chase is about14.37x17.17px. Ivory identification band / graphite nose change the broad cue versus uniformly brown source; fins/nozzle are not individually resolved.
Common-neutral lineup uses unchanged scale1 for new, source, shipped fighter and selected silo. New silhouette remains a small munition, never enlarged into a prop.
Aft closeup resolves fitted lip and inset dark nozzle. Uniform source emission warms the cavity; no flame mesh or animated engine added.
Four cardinal fins are present in binary and visible across aft/extreme views; one thin fin is low-contrast in near-nose-on neutral lighting. Leave contrast/polish to deferred Opus review.
Source pose strips preserve sampled rotations and reset translations ONLY for explicitly labeled diagnostic arrangements. Extreme directions do not introduce flipped, nonuniform or corrective scales.
Launcher closeups preserve actual Silo source pose / sampled opening and actual Sentinel rest-hierarchy mouth root. The latter is not an animated boss replay.
Late salvo Chase frame can leave the viewport. Retained offscreen pair is negative evidence, not a successful visibility claim.
unresolved_limits: No live WebGL/GPU/frame-time test, real shader/postprocessing/particle parity or full-game collision simulation.
Source camera snap rigs and synthetic trajectories, not a recording of a complete play session; source normalized-lerp turn slightly overshoots nominal angular cap in one sample.
Sentinel reference rest pose and first-salvo-slot-only offline visual. Actual receiver integrity and optional pool integration are orchestrator tasks.
Thin fin contrast and tiny-screen feature loss remain deferred polish considerations.
